# v1.2.20 — Top Charts & simpler feedback

## What changed

- **App Store "Top Charts".** If you use the App Store (Glass) theme, Rankings
  now looks and behaves like the real App Store charts: a clean, numbered
  vertical list — rank, cover thumbnail, title, subtitle and the ranking metric
  on the right — grouped into an iOS-style inset list with hairline separators.
  The type filters became an iOS segmented control and the criterion picker an
  iOS select. Dark and Light themes keep the existing card grid, unchanged.
- **Rankings on Home, full charts in their own view.** Home now shows a compact
  **Top 5 preview**. Tap **See All** to open the full **Top Charts** view with
  every criterion (Most Popular, Trending, Top Rated, Most Read, Longest,
  Shortest, Newest, Recently Updated, Best Matches, Most Downloaded, A–Z,
  Completed), type filters, the "My reads" toggle and endless scrolling.
- **No more disliking.** The thumbs-down button is gone. Recommendations are
  driven purely by what you actually read and bookmark, so nothing gets
  silently hidden. (The underlying signal storage is kept dormant for a future
  explicit "Like".)

## Under the hood

- Removed the dislike hard-veto and the dislike weighting from
  `server/recommendation-engine.js`; explicit **likes** still boost titles.
- Rankings rendering is now theme-aware: App Store themes get the numbered
  Top Charts list (`.chart-row`), other themes get the card grid.
- Switching themes re-renders the rankings immediately, so the presentation
  always matches the active theme.
- The full Top Charts list lives in a dedicated `#view-rankings` view with its
  own pagination and infinite scroll.
- Kept `user_signals` table and the `POST/GET /api/user/signals` endpoints
  intact but unused by the UI, ready for a future Like feature.
- Updated the engine, rankings-view and App Store theme test suites.
